title: How Deep Research Works - Mukund Sridhar & Aarush Selvan, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: A Google DeepMind PM and engineer describe how Gemini's Deep Research agent handles long-running multi-minute tasks: iterative planning over partial information, robust state management to survive intermediate failures, and context management via recency bias plus RAG over older 'research notes'. They also emphasize surfacing a plan for user steering and showing sources for trust.

takeaways.what_they_do: They treat multi-minute jobs making many LLM and service calls as inherently failure-prone and build explicit state management so a single intermediate failure doesn't drop the whole task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: being able to build a good state management solution being able to recover from errors effectively so that you just don't drop the whole research uh task due to one failure

takeaways.technique: Recency bias + RAG over older notes
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep full detail for current and recent steps, but compress older task history into 'research notes' stored in a RAG index the model can still query selectively.
takeaways.evidence_quote: as you get to older tasks we kind of selectively pick out uh you know things what we call as research notes and put it in a rag
Gemini will actually put together a research plan for you and present it in a card ... a research plan that they can edit and engage with

takeaways.what_they_do: The model explicitly reasons about which subproblems can run in parallel versus which are inherently sequential, then grounds next steps on partial results found so far.

takeaways.technique: Show sources read vs sources used
takeaways.what_they_do: They surface all sources read and separately those actually used in the output, keeping unused ones in context for follow-ups and citations.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we try and always show as all the sources we read as well as all the sources we used in the report
